speaker: Doctor
text: How long has this swelling and pain in your right ring finger been progressing? Have you noticed any redness or warmth in the area?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds like a traumatic injury. Did you experience any audible snap or pop at the moment of impact? Also, can you make a full straight fist with the injured finger without significant pain?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That inability to flex the distal joint while the finger remains extended is a classic "mallet finger" presentation. Did you notice the fingertip drooping immediately after the injury, or did it stay straight?

REQUEST TEST: X-Ray_right_hand
REQUEST IMAGES: X-Ray_right_hand

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: No bone fractures or dislocations visible. Soft tissue swelling noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger (Avulsion of the Extensor Tendon at the Distal Phalanx). The imaging confirms the absence of a fracture, which typically points to a tendon avulsion rather than a bony injury in the context of your inability to actively extend the fingertip.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
